correctness.rationale: The first image divided by the section size is exactly the sum of a linear term and a singular power term. For sufficiently small parameters, that image lies above the section lower endpoint uniformly over the full section. Subsequent linear contraction gives an exact ceiling formula for the first return and its normalized location. On every fixed logarithmic parameter phase, an additive logarithmic remainder vanishes pointwise away from a null lattice-resonance set, producing almost-sure time and location convergence. The logarithmic transform of the uniform initial coordinate is an exact shifted exponential random variable. Its integer strips give every phase tail and, by a Jacobian change of variables, the same normalized power-law return-location density on every complete strip. Thus the integer duration deficit and return coordinate are conditionally independent. At any interior tail threshold the implicit-function theorem gives the signed first correction. A geometric left-tail estimate supplies uniform integrability and the exact limiting mean. The verification script passes rational square-root orbit and moment calculations plus a floating-point threshold check; these are consistency tests, not a proof of the full theorem.

value.rationale: The originating map comes with a natural vanishing return section whose pointwise return lengths are central to its grazing bifurcation analysis. The full phase-resolved joint probability of return duration and location for a geometric normal-form family is a motivated invariant of transient first-excursion sampling, not an arbitrary parameter slice. A nontrivial conditional factorization yields a geometric duration law and independent power-law location kernel, and the first finite-scale correction quantifies departure from the limiting law. This exact classification is useful for studying induced-return ensembles even without proving a stationary invariant-measure law. Reproducibility alone is not the justification; the value is the new natural joint/statistical structure.
